record.original_question: htop = hLiou for a metric of negative curvature on a compact manifold if and only if it is locally symmetric.

evidence.quote: htop = hLiou for a metric of negative curvature on a compact manifold if and only if it is locally symmetric.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature, and let $\phi_t \colon T^1 M \to T^1 M$ denote the geodesic flow on its unit tangent bundle. Two natural dynamical invariants are associated to this flow:

(1) The topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$, defined as the exponential growth rate of the number of $(\varepsilon,T)$-separated orbit segments of length $T$ as $T \to \infty$ (equivalently, the exponential growth rate of the volume of balls in the universal cover).

(2) The Liouville (measure-theoretic) entropy $h_{\mathrm{Liou}}(g)$, defined as the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $\phi_t$ with respect to the normalized Liouville measure on $T^1 M$ induced by $g$.

By the variational principle, $h_{\mathrm{Liou}}(g) \le h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$, with equality if and only if the Liouville measure is the measure of maximal entropy.

Prove or disprove the following rigidity statement: for every closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of negative sectional curvature,
$$h_{\mathrm{top}}(g) = h_{\mathrm{Liou}}(g) \iff (M,g) \text{ is locally symmetric}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture. It was proved by Katok for surfaces (dimension 2). In higher dimensions it remains open in general; recent work (2024) establishes the conjecture in a $C^2$-neighborhood of real and complex hyperbolic metrics on closed manifolds of dimension $\ge 3$, but the global statement remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Katok's entropy conjecture near real and complex hyperbolic metrics
status_evidence.snippet: Given a real or complex hyperbolic metric on a closed manifold of dimension n ≥ 3, there exists a neighborhood of the metric in the space of negatively curved metrics such that topological entropy and Liouville entropy coincide if and only if the metrics are homothetic.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture proved locally near hyperbolic metrics; the general higher-dimensional case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Fifty years of entropy in dynamics: 1958–2007
status_evidence.snippet: Katok's survey discusses the conjecture that h_top = h_Liou for a negatively curved metric iff it is locally symmetric, established in dimension 2.
status_evidence.claim: Known in dimension 2 (Katok); open in higher dimensions.
